sourceChecks.scope: Direct WebFetch of the article returned HTTP 403 on three attempts (the canonical URL, the numeric-only URL variant, and a SportsEngine syndication mirror, which returned only nav/header boilerplate with no article body). Obtained verbatim quoted content instead via two independent WebSearch queries that returned matching direct quotes from the actual article, attributed to Seth Appert (USA Hockey NTDP U-18 head coach): 'one thing you need to have for the proper angle is momentum back toward your net' and defenders should 'skate at the ice the opponent wants, not at the player, to take away their good ice and force them to bad ice.' This confirms the source genuinely supports the scene's core teaching idea (angle to force the carrier toward worse ice/the boards while keeping backward recovery momentum toward the defended net) -- matching this scenario's objective and q7/q10 feedback almost exactly. I did NOT view the full article body, its structure, or confirm the exact 'A Proper Angle' subheading verbatim (only the quoted sentences above were confirmed); I also did not confirm any U13-specific claim -- the quoted coaching voice is elite/U18-level, applied here only as a general, age-scaled transferable principle, consistent with the source catalog's own disclaimer for this entry ('supports the stated coaching principle... not source-certified').
sourceChecks.claim: Approaching a puck carrier at an angle that forces them toward worse ice (the boards) while retaining backward recovery momentum toward one's own net is a real, attributed USA Hockey coaching principle; it is a general tactical principle, not a U13-specific rule or drill.
